reviews.body:
Thanks for the detailed repro in #9008 and for naming the Nova and gpt-oss gaps up front. The event list made it quick to check this branch against live Bedrock streams.

It holds up on live traffic: 12 recorded `invoke_model_with_response_stream` streams now aggregate to exactly what the anthropic SDK builds from the same events. One delta type is still dropped. With document citations enabled, `_apply_delta` has no branch for `citations_delta`, so cited text blocks keep the empty `"citations": []` copied from `content_block_start` (main had no `citations` key at all). Two-line suggestion inline; happy for it to be a follow-up if you'd rather keep this PR to tool_use and thinking.

| live stream, us-east-1 | main `9ff7c16` | this branch `d50c765` | + suggestion |
|---|---|---|---|
| tool only, two tools, no-arg tool, cut off by `max_tokens` × Haiku 4.5 / Sonnet 4.6 (thinking) / Sonnet 5.5 | 0/12 match | 12/12 | 12/12 |
| document with `citations: {"enabled": true}`, Haiku 4.5 + Sonnet 4.6: cited blocks kept | 0/4 | 0/4 | 4/4 |

The Haiku 4.5 citations stream on this branch:

```
event: {"type": "content_block_delta", "index": 0, "delta": {"type": "citations_delta", "citation": {"type": "char_location", "cited_text": "The sky is blue. ", ...}}}
span:  [{"citations": [], "type": "text", "text": "The sky is blue."}, {"type": "text", "text": " "}, {"citations": [], "type": "text", "text": "Water boils at 100 degrees Celsius at sea level."}]
non-streamed invoke_model, same body: 2 text blocks with citations
```

<details><summary>How I checked, a test for the suggestion, and what looked fine</summary>

Each stream was recorded once with plain boto3 (the `chunk.bytes` items the stream wrapper collects), along with a non-streamed `invoke_model` call on the same body. The items were then replayed through `aggregate_chunks_to_dataclass` on main, on this branch, and on this branch plus the suggestion. "Match" means the same block list (type, text, thinking and signature, tool id/name/input) as `anthropic.lib.streaming._messages.accumulate_event` produces over the same events. In all 12, the non-streamed reply also has the same block types and tool name/input.

```
RED   main src + this PR's tests            4 failed, 8 passed
GREEN this branch, tests/unit/integrations/bedrock   54 passed
RED   this branch + test below              1 failed: {'citations': [], ...} != {..., 'citations': [{'type': 'char_location', ...}]}
GREEN this branch + suggestion + test       55 passed
      ruff 0.14.14 check/format clean, mypy 1.19.1 clean on claude.py
```

```python
    def test_aggregate_chunks__text_with_citations__citations_logged(self):
        citation = {
            "type": "char_location",
            "cited_text": "The sky is blue. ",
            "document_index": 0,
            "document_title": "Facts",
            "start_char_index": 20,
            "end_char_index": 37,
        }
        events = [
            {
                "type": "content_block_start",
                "index": 0,
                "content_block": {"citations": [], "type": "text", "text": ""},
            },
            {
                "type": "content_block_delta",
                "index": 0,
                "delta": {"type": "citations_delta", "citation": citation},
            },
            {
                "type": "content_block_delta",
                "index": 0,
                "delta": {"type": "text_delta", "text": "The sky is blue."},
            },
            {"type": "content_block_stop", "index": 0},
        ]

        response = chunks_aggregator.aggregate_chunks_to_dataclass(
            _content_stream(events, stop_reason="end_turn")
        )

        assert response.native_response["content"] == [
            {"type": "text", "text": "The sky is blue.", "citations": [citation]}
        ]
```

Looked fine:

- Cut off by `max_tokens`: for the truncated call Bedrock streamed only `partial_json: ""` (Haiku 4.5, Sonnet 4.6), so the span gets `input: {}`, which is also what the non-streamed reply returns. The raw-string fallback still covers a stream that is cut mid-JSON.
- Sonnet 5.5 sent a signature-only thinking block (`"thinking": ""`). It is kept, since only empty text blocks are filtered.
- 146 of 146 `content_block_*` events carried an int `index`.
- #9011 calls the public `aggregate_converse_stream_chunks`, which this PR keeps. With both branches merged locally, `tests/unit/integrations/bedrock` gives 58 passed.

</details>

Thank you, @pcbeingused333, for the clear repro in #9008 and the quick turnarounds, and thank you, @kimnamu, for checking it against live Bedrock streams and catching `citations_delta`. Rebuilding the blocks by index makes the streamed Claude output match the non-streamed one, and moving the tool-input parser into `bedrock/tool_input.py` keeps Converse and invoke_model consistent. The logic looks right to me; a few small things that would make the tests stronger:

1. `test_claude_aggregator.py`: `test_aggregate_chunks__tool_call_without_arguments__input_is_empty_object` and `test_aggregate_chunks__tool_input_cut_off__raw_input_kept` check only `content[0]["input"]`. Comparing the whole `native_response` (role, content, stop_reason, usage) in these and the other new tests would also pin the stop reason and usage paths.
2. A few cases the new code handles but no test covers:
   - two tool_use blocks streamed in one turn (each accumulates its own `partial_json` by index)
   - a `redacted_thinking` block (start event only, passed through as is)
   - a delta that arrives without a `content_block_start` (the fallback at `claude.py:101`)
   - an empty text block before a tool_use, which is dropped (`claude.py:159-165`)

Minor:
- `claude.py:102-104` stores a `tool_inputs` entry for every delta, including text and thinking blocks. It's harmless because of the type check at `:153`, but updating it only for `partial_json` deltas would read more clearly.
- Random ids and names in the new tests, instead of fixed literals, would match how the rest of the suite builds data.
- Since citations are now kept too, the title could say `keep tool_use, thinking and citation blocks in Bedrock invoke_model Claude streams`.

Thank you, @pcbeingused333, for taking every point on board so quickly, and thank you again, @kimnamu, for the live-stream check. The tests now pin the whole response and usage for each block shape (interleaved tool calls, redacted thinking, a delta without a start event, the dropped empty text block), and `tool_inputs` only tracks tool-call deltas. Approving.

review_comments.body: ### Duplicate tool-input parser diverges across Bedrock APIs `_parse_tool_input` duplicates the Bedrock parser, so future fixes to streamed tool-input handling can diverge between APIs; move it to a shared Bedrock utility and import it from both aggregators, keeping only API-specific logging at the boundary. Want Baz to fix this for you? [Activate Fixer](https://baz.co/agents/baz)
Moved it to `bedrock/tool_input.py` in d50c765799; both aggregators import it and pass their own logger, so failures are still logged under the API they came from.

A `citations_delta` (`{"type": "citations_delta", "citation": {...}}`) has no branch here and falls through to the debug log, so a cited block keeps the `"citations": []` from its `content_block_start`. Appending the citation, as the anthropic SDK's stream accumulator does, gives the non-streamed shape (4 of 4 cited blocks on the live streams in the summary):

```suggestion
    elif "partial_json" in delta:
        tool_input += delta["partial_json"]
    elif "citation" in delta:
        block["citations"] = (block.get("citations") or []) + [delta["citation"]]
```

Thanks @kimnamu, good catch. Applied in 9e60ec3325: `_apply_delta` now appends each `citation` to the block's `citations`, and your test is added as `test_aggregate_chunks__text_with_citations__citations_logged`. It fails without the change and passes with it; `tests/unit/integrations/bedrock` gives 55 passed, and ruff check/format are clean.

comments.body:
Thanks for the review. Pushed in 87b267a:

1. The tests in `TestClaudeStreamContentBlocks` now compare the whole `native_response` (role, content, stop_reason) and `response.usage`. Usage lives on the response rather than inside `native_response`, so each test asserts both.
2. New cases: two `tool_use` blocks in one turn with interleaved deltas, a `redacted_thinking` block (start event only, passed through), a delta without a `content_block_start`, and an empty text block before a `tool_use` (dropped).
3. `tool_inputs` is now updated only for `partial_json` deltas.
4. Ids, names, text and arguments in these tests use `random_chars` from `tests/conftest.py`.

Title updated to mention citations. `tests/unit/integrations/bedrock`: 59 passed; ruff clean.
